title: Paged weight eviction and safetensors adapter
content:
Purpose
This doc proposes a lightweight, quota-aware paged weight subsystem plus a safetensors file adapter to enable low-latency, memory-efficient model serving across constrained GPU footprints. Goal is to support:
- On-demand (lazy) loading of weight pages at sub-tensor granularity.
- Memory-mapped safetensors as the canonical on-disk format for hosted and private deployments.
- A bounded eviction strategy so active sequences + KV cache maintain SLOs.
- A hot-swap path (layer or shard level) that is safe for in-flight requests.

Constraints and assumptions
- Common target hardware: A100/RTX-like GPU with 40–80GB device RAM and nodes with 256–1024GB host RAM.
- Most models will be converted to safetensors file layout with contiguous weight blocks per layer.
- Batching and KV cache behavior are controlled by existing scheduler and cache subsystems; this design must interoperate without major rework.
- We must not rely on privileged OS features (no custom kernel modules). mmap + madvise allowed.

Key concepts and terminology
- page: contiguous chunk of a weight tensor (e.g., 8–64MiB) that can be loaded/evicted independently.
- residency map: per-model bitmap/tracking structure marking which pages are resident on device or pinned.
- pager: runtime component that ensures pages needed by current executions are resident by issuing async DMA copies (host->device).
- eviction manager: reclaims device pages based on LRU-ish heuristics, sequence pinning, and SLOs.
- safetensors adapter: file reader that exposes file-backed page offsets and handles alignment for device transfers.

Design overview
We introduce a PagedWeights layer under the runtime that sits below the kernel layer selection logic. The kernel requests pointers to weight pages; if missing, the pager ensures residency and returns pointers or a small stall token. High-level flow:
1) Loader converts model file (hf or local) to a sharded safetensors layout (if not already). Metadata file contains page table (tensor -> list of offset,size,preferred-compression-flag).
2) On model load, VM allocates residency map and lightweight descriptors (no weight bytes copied yet).
3) First kernel touch triggers pager async memcpy. For synchronous paths we allow a short stall (configurable 1–5ms).
4) Pager attempts to prefetch sibling pages when access patterns (layer sequential access) are detected.
5) Eviction manager reclaims pages subject to policy, but never evicts pages pinned by in-flight sequences or by high-priority routes.

Safetensors adapter details
- File layout expectation: per-tensor table with offset/length aligned to 4k pages. We will include an optional per-page checksum for quiet corruption detection.
- Adapter exposes two interfaces: get_page_descriptors(model_id, tensor, page_idx) -> list[string offsets] and open_page_stream(offset, size) -> host-mapped pointer.
- Use POSIX mmap on host side for zero-copy into staging area; then submit cudaMemcpyAsync from host-mapped region to device buffer. For private/on-prem where NVME read is faster, allow direct pinned IO to avoid double-copy (experimental).

Page size and alignment heuristics
- Default page size: 16MiB. Rationale: balance between DMA setup overhead and eviction granularity.
- Allow model-level override: small models may use 4MiB; very large layers can be split into 64MiB pages.
- Align offsets to 4KiB for mmap + OS alignment.

Pager behavior and prefetch strategy
- On first touch: issue async transfer for the page. If page needed immediately, kube the request and allow a configurable short stall (also used as circuit breaker).
- Prefetch window: observe sequential access across layers. If same execution touches page i of layer L, paginate to prefetch i+1 and i+2 of L and first page of L+1.
- Adaptive prefetch: track hit/miss ratio per model and increase/decrease window.
- Priority queue: pager prioritizes pages for active sequences by priority (route, SLA). Background prefetches are lower priority and can be preempted.

Residency tracking and pin semantics
- Each in-flight request binds to a set of pages (pinned) until sequence commit/response complete. Pin count increments on kernel start and decrements on finish.
- KV cache pages (past key/values): considered high value; eviction manager treats them similarly to pinned pages but can be truncated (configurable) to reclaim memory under pressure.
- Weight residency table also maintains last-access timestamp for eviction heuristics.

Eviction policy
- Multilevel policy:
  * never-evict set: small set of critical pages pinned by admin/ML engineers (config per-model).
  * pinned pages: pages currently used by in-flight sequences (immovable until completion).
  * soft-pinned pages: KV cache pages with decaying priority; can be reclaimed gradually (truncate oldest keys).
  * LRU bucket: remaining pages evicted based on recency weighted by page hotness and estimated reload cost.
- Eviction is conservative: we only evict when device free < threshold (configurable, default 12% free). Also maintain emergency reserve for high-priority routes.
- Eviction should trigger proactive prefetches for likely-needed pages to avoid cascaded misses.

Interaction with scheduling and kernels
- Kernels call a kernel_helper->ensure_weights_resident(tensor, page_ids, deadline) before compute. The helper returns status: resident | pending_async | failed.
- Scheduler integrates pager latency into per-request latency budget. If pager signals likely miss, scheduler may: reduce batch size, re-route to a cached model variant, or deny new requests.
- For streaming/token-at-a-time workloads, we pin causal KV pages per request and allow weight pager to operate in background. Use a fast-path when whole model fits in device memory.

Hot-swap and versioning
- Support hot-swap at shard/layer granularity: new model version provides replacement safetensors files with page table mapping.
- Swap protocol: mark model variant as LATEST, start new loader in parallel, warm up prefetched pages on spare capacity, then atomically update model pointer for new requests. Old in-flight requests continue using previous residency mapping until completion.
- Rollback: maintain both residency maps until old map has zero pins, then release pages.

APIs and config knobs (examples)
- Model manifest fields: page_size, mandatory_pages (list of tensor names), checksum_per_page, preferred_page_order.
- Runtime flags: pager_stall_ms (default 3), prefetch_window_min, prefetch_window_max, eviction_threshold_percent, emergency_reserve_percent.
- Admin API: pin_page(model, tensor, page_idx), unpin_page(...), list_residency(model), force_eviction(model, bytes)

Metrics to emit
- page_misses_total, page_hits_total, avg_page_load_latency_ms, pages_evicted_total, pages_prefetched_total, page_checksum_failures_total, pinned_page_bytes, device_free_bytes_triggers.
- Per-model hit rate and per-route miss-impact (latency tail correlation).

Operational concerns
- Corruption: verify optional per-page checksums at load and periodically. If checksum fails, mark model as corrupt and fail new requests for safety.
- Thundering herd: when a hot layer is cold (evicted), many tokens might request page simultaneously. Use leader-election per-page touch: first requester triggers load, others wait on condition variable with a short backoff jitter.
- Memory accounting: integrate with existing allocator so pager does not exceed device pool. Host staging allocations must be bounded per node.

Performance experiments (planned)
1) Page size sweep (4, 8, 16, 32MiB) with a 7B dense transformer on A100, measure avg+tail latency for 2–16 token streaming.
2) Prefetch window sensitivity with synthetic interleaved layer access.
3) Eviction threshold impact on throughput under multi-tenant noisy neighbors.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Use of device-side pageable memory (cudaHostRegister + GPUDirect) vs explicit host->device memcpy: simplifies code but less portable.
- Compression of pages (quantized on disk): increases CPU decode and host->device time; need benchmark.
- How aggressive should we be evicting KV cache vs weights? Workloads differ. Potential heuristic: weight hotness > KV hit rate -> keep weight.
- Interaction with model compilation kernels that expect contiguous device buffers: we may need temporary gather buffers if kernel cannot handle paged layouts.

Risks
- Added complexity in runtime and subtle bugs in pinning can cause incorrect inference results or memory leaks.
- Tail latency regression if pager misses are frequent.

Next steps / short roadmap
- Prototype safetensors adapter + residency map in C++ runtime (2w).
- Minimal pager with page-level mmap + cudaMemcpyAsync and a simple LRU eviction (3w).
- Integrate leader election for thundering herd protection + metrics (2w).
- Run performance sweep and adjust default page size and thresholds (2w).

Notes and references
- See INF-3421 for earlier pager spikes analysis.
- Related: paging interacts closely with KV cache eviction plans in eng-serving-runtime/kv-cache-eviction.md (refer to linked confluence page).
